div.head: Abt 87
div.ab: Gif esnes eage ⁊ foot of weorðeþ aslagen, ealne weorðe hine forgelde.
Gif esnes eage ⁊ foot of weorðeþ aslagen, ealne weorþe hine forgelde.
Gif esnes eage ⁊ foot of weorðeþ aslagen, ealne weorðe hine forgelde.
Wenn eines Lohnknechts Auge und Fuss abgehauen werden, entgelte ihn [der Thäter dem Herrn] ganz mit [Knechts-]Werth.
If a hired servant’s eye and foot are struck off, let [the offender] pay for him [to the master] in full with [a servant’s] value.
If the eye and foot of a servant are destroyed [by blows], his full value shall be paid.
If a servant’s eye or foot is destroyed, the full value is to be paid for him.
If a servant’s eye or foot becomes struck off, let him pay him [i.e., the servant’s master] the entire worth.

note.seg: ‘und’ hier = ‘oder’ (s. o. 9⁵), da auch beim Freien Fuß + Auge ganzem Wergeld gleichkommt. Hier soll gesagt sein, dass jede jener Verstümmelungen den unfreien Arbeiter dem Herrn wertlos mache, also ganzen Esne-Wert koste.

‘and’ here = ‘or’ (see above 9⁵), since even for a free man foot + eye equal the whole wergild. The point here is that each of those mutilations makes the unfree labourer worthless to his lord, and therefore costs the whole value of the esne.
Zu foot s. 72²; vgl. Gl Fuss 4
On foot see 72²; cf. Gl Fuss 4
Liebermann translates and as meaning ‘or’ (cf. cap. 9 above, Ine, cap. 27, etc.).

note.label: worth.
note.seg: ⁊ can mean either ‘and’ or ‘or’; the latter seems more likely here, but see discussion in Commentary under ‘Servants.’ Other adversative uses of this ligature can be found in §§15, 23, 30.
